principles.summary: Be aware of excessive praise, hypercriticism, and slander as signs of envy. Ignore their behavior and do not try to help or do favors for those who envy you.

principles.name: Destroy Envy's Source
principles.summary: Reveal a harmless defect in your character to disarm envy. Destroy its source by not giving it fuel.

principles.name: Act Before Envy Takes Root
principles.summary: Address envy before it becomes a problem by being proactive and not letting it take hold.

principles.name: Use Envy to Your Advantage
principles.summary: Turn envy into a tool for your own success by using it to motivate you to achieve more.

principles.name: Display Contempt for the Envious
principles.summary: Displaying contempt for those who envy you can be an effective way to deal with their negative emotions.

principles.name: Use Good Fortune to Punish the Envious
principles.summary: Your success and good fortune can be used as a form of punishment for those who envy you.

principles.name: Convert Envy into a Heroic Revenge
principles.summary: The best revenge against those who envy you is to achieve greatness and let your accomplishments speak for themselves.

principles.name: Don't Overextend After Victory
principles.summary: When you achieve success, be cautious and consolidate your gains. Don't push too far, as this can lead to overextension and loss of power.

principles.name: Recognize the Role of Circumstance
principles.summary: Understand that your success is often due to specific circumstances, and don't repeat the same actions in similar situations.

principles.name: Don't Let Success Go to Your Head
principles.summary: Avoid arrogance and overconfidence after achieving success. Stay humble and vigilant, as this is often the moment of greatest peril.

principles.name: Consolidate Your Power Base
principles.summary: After achieving success, focus on consolidating your power base and recognizing the role of luck and circumstance in your success.

principles.name: Be Aware of the Dangers of Overconfidence
principles.summary: Recognize that success can make you more hostile and emotional, leading to poor decision-making.

principles.name: Play the Courtier's Game
principles.summary: After achieving success, play the courtier's game by paying attention to the laws of power and adapting to changing circumstances.

principles.name: Control Your Emotions After Success
principles.summary: After achieving success, it's essential to control your emotions and not let them cloud your judgment.

principles.name: Recognize the Role of Luck and Circumstance
principles.summary: Luck and circumstance play a significant role in achieving success, and it's essential to acknowledge this.

principles.name: Vary Your Rhythms and Patterns
principles.summary: To maintain power and success, it's essential to vary your rhythms and patterns.

principles.name: Be Merciless with Your Enemy
principles.summary: When you've achieved victory, it's essential to be merciless with your enemy and crush them into nonexistence.

principles.name: Don't Overreach After Victory
principles.summary: After achieving victory, it's essential to avoid overreaching and advancing against others unnecessarily.

principles.name: Stop with a Victory
principles.summary: When you've achieved success, it's essential to stop and walk away, rather than risking lessening the effect or ending up defeated.

principles.name: Assume Formlessness
principles.summary: To protect yourself, be adaptable and on the move, like water.

principles.name: Avoid Rigid Systems
principles.summary: Rigid systems can become a dead end, slowing you down and making you vulnerable to attack.

principles.name: Use Mobility to Outmaneuver
principles.summary: Mobility is key to success in war and in life.

principles.name: Don't Bet on Stability
principles.summary: Nothing in the world can remain stable forever.

principles.name: Use the Size of the Board to Your Advantage
principles.summary: In a large and complex environment, use your opponent's rigidity against them.

principles.name: Adapt to Circumstances
principles.summary: As you age, be prepared to change your approach to maintain relevance and power. This means discarding outdated ideas and strategies, and being open to new perspectives. As Napoleon said, 'The laws that govern circumstances are abolished by new circumstances.'

principles.name: Avoid Rigidity
principles.summary: Rigidity can make you appear outdated and inflexible, leading to a loss of power and influence. Instead, cultivate a sense of formlessness, which allows you to adapt and respond to changing circumstances.

principles.name: Use Formlessness Strategically
principles.summary: Formlessness can be a powerful tool for gaining the upper hand in situations where predictability is an advantage. By appearing unpredictable, you can keep your enemies off balance and create opportunities for surprise attacks.

principles.name: Concentrate Power When Necessary
principles.summary: While formlessness can be a powerful tool, it's also important to know when to concentrate your power and strike with force. This can be a key to achieving victory in situations where predictability is an advantage.

principles.name: Be Like a Chameleon
principles.summary: Conform on the surface while breaking down your enemy from the inside. This allows you to catch them off guard and succeed at a strategy that rigid people are helpless against.

principles.name: Avoid Sacrificing Mobility for Size
principles.summary: The flexible and fleet of foot will almost always win, for they have more strategic options. The more gigantic the enemy, the easier it is to induce collapse. Be like a vapor, elusive and swift.

principles.name: Be Vigilant of Your Character's Form
principles.summary: As you get older, you must rely less on the past and be vigilant lest your character's form makes you seem a relic. This is the first sign of decrepitude and predictability.

principles.name: Encircle the Enemy's Brain
principles.summary: Use mind games, propaganda, and irritation tactics to confuse and dishearten your opponent. As the Chinese military strategist said, 'Use the size of the board to your advantage, spreading out in every direction so that your opponent cannot fathom your movements in a simple linear way.'

principles.name: Train Yourself to be Formless
principles.summary: To be powerful, one must be adaptable and flexible, like water. Never show a clear form, as it can be attacked. Train yourself to take nothing personally and never let anyone get your back up. This allows you to infuriate and disorient your opponents.

principles.name: Avoid Being Predictable
principles.summary: Predictability makes you appear comical and weak. As you get older, you must rely less on the past and be vigilant lest your character's form makes you seem a relic. Be like a vapor, elusive and swift.

principles.name: Use Indirectness to Your Advantage
principles.summary: Indirectness and elusiveness yield better results at a lower cost. Use the size of the board to your advantage, spreading out in every direction to confuse your opponent. This is the ultimate form of strategy.

principles.name: Don't Rely on Others' Ideas
principles.summary: Too much reliance on others' ideas and advice can lead to a loss of autonomy and power. Instead, trust your own judgment and be willing to challenge conventional wisdom.

principles.name: Study the Classics
principles.summary: The classics provide valuable insights and lessons that can be applied to various fields, including politics, business, and war. As Robert Greene notes, 'The classics are the foundation of all knowledge.'

principles.name: Seek Out Knowledge from Unconventional Sources
principles.summary: Unconventional sources can provide unique skills and insights that can be applied to various situations.

principles.name: Understand the Power of Deception
principles.summary: Deception can be a powerful tool in achieving one's goals, but it must be used carefully and strategically.

principles.name: Learn from History's Great Leaders
principles.summary: Great leaders provide valuable lessons and insights that can be applied to various situations.

principles.name: Seek Out Knowledge from Multiple Disciplines
principles.summary: Studying multiple disciplines can provide a deeper understanding of the world and develop more effective strategies.
